title: Title & Registration Services Temporary Tags: State Reference Sheet and Issuing Rules
content:
## State reference

| Registration state | Original-tag validity (days from the handover date) | State maximum extensions |
|---|---|---|
| AZ | 30 | 1 |
| TX | 60 | 1 |
| GA | 30 | 2 |
| FL | 30 | 1 |
| NC | 30 | 1 |
| OH | 45 | 1 |
| PA | 90 | 1 |
| CO | 60 | 2 |

## Issuing rules

1. Under Title & Registration Services the original temporary tag is issued at handover, valid for the registration state's original-tag validity days counted from the handover date.
2. A tag is issued only while the order's status is awaiting documents, ready to submit, submitted or rejected; once registration is issued no tag is issued.
3. An extension tag is issued only when the current tag expires before registration is expected, and only on or before the current tag's expiration date recorded on the order. The tag date is compared as a calendar date; an extension on the expiration date itself is allowed and an extension the day after is not. No days after the expiration date are allowed for an extension.
4. An extension can be issued from the service type's extension request lead days before that date.
5. When the service type requires documents complete for extensions, no extension tag is issued while the order is awaiting the customer's documents.
6. Extension tags used must stay below the lower of the service type's limit and the registration state's maximum extensions.
7. The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis for sizing extension tags: "An extension tag is valid for the service's extension tag validity days from its issue date, unless the state's original-tag validity is larger, in which case that applies."
8. Each tag has its own sequence number (the original is 1, the first extension 2, and so on), and the order always records the tag currently on the vehicle.

The expiration date relied on in rule 3 is the one recorded on the order for the current tag, not a date the customer reports.

## Rule 3 and rule 4 at their boundaries (hypothetical dates, 7-day lead)

| Current tag's expiration date on the order | Requested extension date | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 20 May | 12 May | before the lead period opens; not yet issuable |
| 20 May | 13 May | within the lead period |
| 20 May | 20 May | allowed, the expiration date itself |
| 20 May | 21 May | not allowed, the day after expiration |

## Rule 6 illustrated (hypothetical)

An order registering in GA (state maximum 2) under a service type whose own limit is 1 can carry at most 1 extension tag: with 0 extensions used, one may be issued; with 1 used, none. Registering in CO (state maximum 2) under a service type whose own limit is 3, the lower figure is 2.

## Status test (rule 2)

| Order status | Tag may be issued |
|---|---|
| awaiting documents, ready to submit, submitted, rejected | yes |
| registered, completed, cancelled | no |

superseded_clauses: An extension tag is valid for the service's extension tag validity days from its issue date, unless the state's original-tag validity is larger, in which case that applies.
